arxiv-2203-10933.title: Global energy preserving model reduction for multi-symplectic PDEs
arxiv-2203-10933.creator: Murat Uzunca, Bülent Karasözen, Ayhan Aydın
arxiv-2203-10933.description: Abstract Many Hamiltonian systems can be recast in multi-symplectic form. We develop a reduced-order model (ROM) for multi-symplectic Hamiltonian partial differential equations (PDEs) that preserves the global energy. The full-order solutions are obtained by finite difference discretization in space and the global energy preserving average vector field (AVF) method.

arxiv-2308-00682.title: TimePool: Visually Answer “Which and When” Questions On Univariate Time Series
arxiv-2308-00682.creator: Tinghao Feng Appalachian State University, Yueqi Hu UNC Charlotte, Jing Yang UNC Charlotte, Tom Polk Compass Draw, LLC, Ye Zhao Kent State University, Shixia Liu Tshinghua University, Zhaocong Yang UNC Charlotte
arxiv-2308-00682.description: Abstract When exploring time series datasets, analysts often pose “which and when” questions. For example, with world life expectancy data over one hundred years, they may inquire about the top 10 countries in life expectancy and the time period when they achieved this status, or which countries have had longer life expectancy than Ireland and when.

arxiv-2401-17741.title: Haris: an Advanced Autonomous Mobile Robot for Smart Parking Assistance
arxiv-2401-17741.creator: Layth Hamad 1 2 , Muhammad Asif Khan 1 , Hamid Menouar 1 , Fethi Filali 1 , and Amr Mohamed 2
arxiv-2401-17741.description: Abstract This paper presents Haris, an advanced autonomous mobile robot system for tracking the location of vehicles in crowded car parks using license plate recognition. The system employs simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) for autonomous navigation and precise mapping of the parking area, eliminating the need for GPS dependency.

arxiv-2402-13430.title: LinkSAGE: Optimizing Job Matching Using Graph Neural Networks DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ; August 25–29, 2024; Barcelona, Spain ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks CCS: Human-centered computing Social networking sites CCS: Information systems Recommender
arxiv-2402-13430.creator: Ping Liu, Haichao Wei, Xiaochen Hou, Jianqiang Shen, Shihai He, Kay Qianqi Shen, Zhujun Chen, Fedor Borisyuk, Daniel Hewlett, Liang Wu, Srikant Veeraraghavan, Alex Tsun, Chengming Jiang, Wenjing Zhang
arxiv-2402-13430.description: Abstract . We present LinkSAGE, an innovative framework that integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) into large-scale personalized job matching systems, designed to address the complex dynamics of LinkedIn’s extensive professional network. Our approach capitalizes on a novel job marketplace graph, the largest and most intricate of its kind in industry, with billions of nodes and edges.

arxiv-2409-07094.title: Deep intra-operative illumination calibration of hyperspectral cameras
arxiv-2409-07094.creator: Alexander Baumann, Leonardo Ayala, Alexander Studier-Fischer, Jan Sellner, Berkin Özdemir, Karl-Friedrich Kowalewski, Slobodan Ilic, Silvia Seidlitz, Lena Maier-Hein
arxiv-2409-07094.description: Abstract Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is emerging as a promising novel imaging modality with various potential surgical applications. Currently available cameras, however, suffer from poor integration into the clinical workflow because they require the lights to be switched off, or the camera to be manually recalibrated as soon as lighting conditions change.

arxiv-2410-08286.title: Completely Multipolar Model for Many-Body Water-Ion and Ion-Ion Interactions
arxiv-2410-08286.creator: Joseph P. Heindel, Lukas Kim, Martin Head-Gordon, Teresa Head-Gordon
arxiv-2410-08286.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Joseph P. Heindel, Lukas Kim, Martin Head-Gordon, Teresa Head-Gordon. This work constructs an advanced force field, the Completely Multipolar Model (CMM), to quantitatively reproduce each term of an energy decomposition analysis (EDA) for aqueous solvated alkali metal cations and halide anions and their ion pairings. We find that all individual EDA terms remain well-approximated in the CMM for ion-water and ion-ion interactions, except for polarization, which shows errors due to the partial covalency of ion interactions near their equilibrium.

arxiv-2506-11969.title: A Robust Local Fréchet Regression Using Unbalanced Neural Optimal Transport with Applications to Dynamic Single-cell Genomics Data
arxiv-2506-11969.creator: Binghao Yan, Hongzhe Li
arxiv-2506-11969.description: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies have enabled the profiling of gene expression for a collection of cells across time during a dynamic biological process. Given that each time point provides only a static snapshot, modeling and understanding the underlying cellular dynamics remains a central yet challenging task in modern genomics.

arxiv-2508-07201.title: Propagation Tree Is Not Deep: Adaptive Graph Contrastive Learning Approach for Rumor Detection
arxiv-2508-07201.creator: Chaoqun Cui, Caiyan Jia
arxiv-2508-07201.description: Abstract Rumor detection on social media has become increasingly important. Most existing graph-based models presume rumor propagation trees (RPTs) have deep structures and learn sequential stance features along branches. However, through statistical analysis on real-world datasets, we find RPTs exhibit wide structures, with most nodes being shallow 1-level replies.

arxiv-2510-04751.title: Higher-Order Boundary Conditions for Atomistic Dislocation Simulations Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
arxiv-2510-04751.creator: Xinyi Wei, Julian Braun, Yangshuai Wang, Lei Zhang
arxiv-2510-04751.description: Abstract We present a higher-order boundary condition for atomistic simulations of dislocations that address the slow convergence of standard supercell methods. The method is based on a multipole expansion of the equilibrium displacement, combining continuum predictor solutions with discrete moment corrections.

pmc-10693557.title: Association analysis of production traits of Japanese quail (Coturnix japonica) using restriction-site associated DNA sequencing
pmc-10693557.creator: Mohammad Ibrahim Haqani, Michiharu Nakano, Atsushi J Nagano, Yoshiaki Nakamura, Masaoki Tsudzuki
pmc-10693557.description: This study was designed to perform an association analysis and identify SNP markers associated with production traits of Japanese quail using restriction-site-associated DNA sequencing. pmc-13115258.creator: Stéphanie Girard, Jason D’Amours, Jessica Bélisle, Annabelle Ross, Annie Paquet
pmc-13115258.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Individualized approaches are essential for promoting physical activity participation among children with developmental disabilities.Parental involvement is crucial for physical literacy development of children with developmental disabilities. What are the implications of the main findings? Design programs and interventions that offer flexible, tailored strategies to accommodate each child’s unique abilities, preferences, and support needs.

pmc-13123277.title: Diffusion Wake: A Distinctive Consequence of the Mach-Cone Wake Induced by Supersonic Jets in High-Energy Heavy-Ion Collisions
pmc-13123277.creator: Zhong Yang, Xin-Nian Wang
pmc-13123277.description: In this Research Perspective, we briefly review the diffusion wake, a distinctive consequence of the Mach-cone wake induced by the supersonic jets in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions. The diffusion wake depletes soft hadrons in the direction opposite to the propagating jet.

pmc-13460569.title: Weighted multi-scale and wavelet-enhanced Segment Anything Model for salient object detection
pmc-13460569.creator: Zhe Liu, Dan Tian
pmc-13460569.description: Salient Object Detection (SOD) is concerned with isolating the visually most noticeable objects in an image via precise segmentation. Previous approaches, especially those that adapt the Segment Anything Model (SAM), often yield saliency maps that contain incomplete object masks, blurred boundaries, and a lack of fine-grained details.

pmc-13625362.title: From policy to practice: feasibility and acceptability of training ASHAs to deliver birth preparedness and complication readiness in North Karnataka, India: a pre–post study
pmc-13625362.creator: Annapurna Kari, Mubashir Angolkar
pmc-13625362.description: BackgroundMaternal mortality remains a major public health concern in low-resource settings. Birth preparedness and complication readiness (BPCR) is an established strategy to improve timely care-seeking and reduce preventable maternal and neonatal complications. Utilizing Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) to deliver BPCR interventions may strengthen community-level implementation; however, evidence on feasibility and acceptability is limited.

pmc-13673123.title: Active Helicobacter pylori Infection and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction
pmc-13673123.creator: Mohammed Hashem, Martin O Sundqvist, Jonatan Wärme, Magnus Bäck, Robin Hofmann
pmc-13673123.description: ObjectiveChronic Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection may promote systemic inflammation and has been proposed as a contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF), but clinical evidence is inconsistent. The aim of the study was to explore whether active H. pylori infection was associated with AF in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
